title: Escape to Victory
creator: John Huston
subject: politics
subjectName: POW footballers vs Nazi team
logline: Allied POWs led by Michael Caine and Sylvester Stallone play an exhibition football match against their German captors.
whyItMatters: A star-studded fictionalization of the WWII 'Death Match' legend, cementing football-as-resistance in popular culture.
whereToFind: Available to rent/buy on Prime Video, Apple TV; DVD/Blu-ray in print

title: Bend It Like Beckham
creator: Gurinder Chadha
subject: fans
subjectName: British-Indian teenager pursuing football against family expectations
logline: A British-Indian teenager defies her traditional family's expectations to pursue professional football.
whyItMatters: The highest-grossing British football film, a landmark for South Asian representation and women's football visibility.
whereToFind: Available on Netflix, Prime Video; DVD/Blu-ray widely available

title: The Damned United
creator: Tom Hooper
subject: player
subjectName: Brian Clough's turbulent 44 days managing Leeds United
logline: Dramatizes Brian Clough's disastrous, feud-fueled 44-day tenure as Leeds United manager in 1974.
whyItMatters: Adapted from David Peace's acclaimed novel, it remains one of the sharpest character studies in football cinema.
whereToFind: Available on Prime Video, Apple TV; DVD/Blu-ray in print

title: Shaolin Soccer
creator: Stephen Chow
subject: culture
subjectName: Kung fu monks form a football team
logline: A disgraced footballer recruits Shaolin monks who use martial arts skills to dominate the football pitch.
whyItMatters: One of the highest-grossing Hong Kong films ever, fusing wuxia comedy with football to reach audiences worldwide.
whereToFind: Available on Prime Video, Tubi; DVD widely available

title: Offside
creator: Jafar Panahi
subject: fans
subjectName: Iranian women disguising as men to attend a match
logline: Young Iranian women disguise themselves as men to sneak into a men's World Cup qualifier, defying the stadium ban on women.
whyItMatters: A key work of Iranian social-realist cinema using football to critique gender restrictions, banned domestically for years.
whereToFind: Available on Kanopy, Mubi, Criterion Channel
awards: Silver Bear, Berlin International Film Festival

title: The Miracle of Bern
creator: Sönke Wortmann
subject: nation
subjectName: West Germany's 1954 World Cup win and postwar identity
logline: A boy's reunion with his POW father intertwines with West Germany's stunning 1954 World Cup final victory.
whyItMatters: A defining German film linking football triumph to postwar national healing and identity.
whereToFind: Available on Prime Video (rental), Kanopy; DVD in print
awards: German Film Award for Best Film

title: Looking for Eric
creator: Ken Loach
subject: player
subjectName: A postman's imaginary friendship with Eric Cantona
logline: A depressed Manchester postman finds life advice from an imagined Eric Cantona, who appears as his guiding spirit.
whyItMatters: A rare instance of a working footballer (Cantona) appearing in fiction as himself, blending Loach's social realism with comedy.
whereToFind: Available on Prime Video, Tubi; DVD in print

title: The Cup
creator: Khyentse Norbu
subject: fans
subjectName: Buddhist monks obsessed with watching the World Cup
logline: Young monks at a Himalayan monastery scheme to get a satellite dish to watch the 1998 World Cup final.
whyItMatters: One of the first Bhutanese films ever made, using football fandom to explore modernity's reach into isolated tradition.
whereToFind: Available on Kanopy, Mubi; DVD via Criterion-adjacent distributors

title: You'll Never Walk Alone
creator: Gerry and the Pacemakers (orig. Rodgers & Hammerstein)
subject: club
subjectName: Liverpool FC's terrace anthem
logline: A Broadway show tune adopted by Liverpool's Kop as its defining pre-match anthem since 1963.
whyItMatters: Widely considered football's most famous anthem, later a symbol of Hillsborough remembrance.
whereToFind: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube; original single reissued on multiple compilations

title: World in Motion
creator: New Order with the England squad
subject: nation
subjectName: England's official 1990 World Cup song
logline: Manchester band New Order teamed with the England squad (including John Barnes's rap verse) for the 1990 World Cup song.
whyItMatters: Widely regarded as the best England World Cup song ever, blending indie credibility with terrace anthem status.
whereToFind: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube

title: Three Lions
creator: Baddiel, Skinner and the Lightning Seeds
subject: nation
subjectName: England's Euro 96 anthem, 'Football's Coming Home'
logline: Written for Euro 96, this song became England's default football anthem with its 'It's coming home' refrain.
whyItMatters: One of the most re-released and culturally embedded football songs in English history, revived for nearly every tournament since.
whereToFind: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube
awards: UK Singles Chart No.1 (1996 and 1998 versions)

title: Blue Is the Colour
creator: The Chelsea Football Team
subject: club
subjectName: Chelsea FC's League Cup final single
logline: Chelsea's entire playing squad recorded this single ahead of the 1972 League Cup final, an early club-anthem trend.
whyItMatters: One of the first instances of an English club squad recording its own commercial single, setting a template later copied widely.
whereToFind: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube

title: UEFA Champions League Anthem
creator: Tony Britten (adapted from Handel's Zadok the Priest)
subject: tournament
subjectName: Official Champions League anthem
logline: Adapted from Handel's coronation anthem, this became the instantly recognizable sound of European club football's elite competition.
whyItMatters: Arguably the most globally recognized piece of football-associated music ever composed for a competition.
whereToFind: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube

title: Waka Waka
creator: Shakira featuring Freshlyground
subject: tournament
subjectName: Official song of the 2010 FIFA World Cup
logline: Shakira's official 2010 World Cup song, blending Colombian pop with South African group Freshlyground, became a global hit.
whyItMatters: One of the best-selling World Cup songs ever, closely tied to South Africa's first World Cup on African soil.
whereToFind: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube
awards: MTV Europe Music Award for Best Song

title: Wavin' Flag
creator: K'naan
subject: tournament
subjectName: Coca-Cola's 2010 World Cup promotional anthem
logline: Somali-Canadian rapper K'naan's song became Coca-Cola's global anthem for the 2010 South Africa World Cup.
whyItMatters: Reframed a song about civil war and resilience into one of the tournament's most recognized promotional anthems.
whereToFind: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube

title: The Ball Is Round: A Global History of Football
creator: David Goldblatt
subject: culture
subjectName: Global football history
logline: A sweeping single-volume history tracing football's spread from Victorian England to a global obsession.
whyItMatters: Widely regarded as the definitive one-volume global football history.
whereToFind: Penguin paperback; widely available in bookstores and libraries
awards: William Hill Sports Book of the Year shortlist

title: Inverting the Pyramid: The History of Football Tactics
creator: Jonathan Wilson
subject: tactics
subjectName: Evolution of formations and systems
logline: Traces how football tactics evolved from the 2-3-5 pyramid to modern pressing systems.
whyItMatters: The benchmark English-language book on football tactical history, hugely influential among coaches and writers.
whereToFind: Orion/Nation Books; ebook and paperback widely available

title: Soccer in Sun and Shadow
originalTitle: El fútbol a sol y sombra
creator: Eduardo Galeano (trans. Mark Fried)
subject: culture
subjectName: Lyrical history of World Cup football
logline: A lyrical vignette-based history of football's beauty and politics from a legendary Uruguayan writer.
whyItMatters: Perhaps the most acclaimed literary football book ever written, translated into dozens of languages.
whereToFind: Verso/Nation Books; paperback and ebook widely available
awards: Named one of Sports Illustrated's 100 best sports books

title: Football Against the Enemy
creator: Simon Kuper
subject: politics
subjectName: Football's intersection with global politics
logline: A journalistic tour connecting football to nationalism, war and politics across dozens of countries.
whyItMatters: A pioneering work of football journalism that reframed the sport as a lens on world politics.
whereToFind: Orion; paperback
awards: William Hill Sports Book of the Year 1994

title: How Soccer Explains the World
creator: Franklin Foer
subject: politics
subjectName: Globalization viewed through football
logline: Uses football fandom and clubs worldwide to explore globalization, tribalism and nationalism.
whyItMatters: A bestselling US book that introduced many American readers to football's global political weight.
whereToFind: Harper Perennial; paperback and ebook

title: Fear and Loathing in La Liga: Barcelona vs Real Madrid
creator: Sid Lowe
subject: club
subjectName: Barcelona-Real Madrid rivalry
logline: A history of Spanish football's greatest rivalry, entwined with Catalan and Spanish politics.
whyItMatters: The standard English reference for understanding the Clasico's historical and political depth.
whereToFind: Yellow Jersey Press; paperback and ebook
awards: Football Book of the Year, British Sports Book Awards

title: Diego Maradona
creator: Asif Kapadia
subject: player
subjectName: Diego Maradona
logline: Chronicles Maradona's transcendent and turbulent years at Napoli using exclusive archival footage.
whyItMatters: Won acclaim for humanizing a global icon through unseen personal footage, part of Kapadia's celebrated trilogy.
whereToFind: Available on Max, Apple TV; DVD/Blu-ray in print

title: Sunderland 'Til I Die
creator: Tom Mallion, Leo Pearlman (exec.)
subject: club
subjectName: Sunderland AFC's back-to-back relegations
logline: Tracks Sunderland's painful collapse from Premier League club to League One amid boardroom chaos.
whyItMatters: One of the most acclaimed football docuseries for its unflinching look at footballing decline and community loss.
whereToFind: Available on Netflix

title: The Two Escobars
creator: Jeff Zimbalist, Michael Zimbalist
subject: politics
subjectName: Pablo Escobar's ties to Colombian football and Andrés Escobar's murder
logline: Interweaves drug lord Pablo Escobar's football investments with the tragic murder of national captain Andrés Escobar.
whyItMatters: Part of ESPN's 30 for 30 series, widely considered one of the best sports documentaries ever made about football's dark side.
whereToFind: Available on ESPN+, Netflix (regional)

title: Going to the Match
creator: L.S. Lowry
subject: fans
subjectName: Crowds streaming toward a Northern English football ground
logline: Lowry's signature matchstick-figure style captures the mass ritual of working-class fans heading to a match.
whyItMatters: One of the most beloved British paintings of football culture, purchased by the PFA for record sums at auction.
whereToFind: Professional Footballers' Association collection, on loan to Lowry Centre, Salford
awards: Record UK sporting art auction price (2011)

title: Dynamism of a Soccer Player
creator: Umberto Boccioni
subject: player
subjectName: Futurist depiction of a footballer in motion
logline: Boccioni's Futurist masterpiece fragments a footballer's movement into overlapping planes of color and force.
whyItMatters: A landmark of Italian Futurism using football to embody the movement's obsession with speed, motion and modernity.
whereToFind: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York

title: The Football Players
creator: Henri Rousseau
subject: fans
subjectName: Naive-style painting of men playing football
logline: Rousseau's self-taught Primitivist style renders football players in his signature flat, dreamlike manner.
whyItMatters: One of the earliest major fine-art paintings to take football itself as its subject, by a canonical modern painter.
whereToFind: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York

title: Bobby Moore Statue
creator: Philip Jackson
subject: player
subjectName: England's 1966 World Cup-winning captain
logline: A 20-foot bronze statue of England's World Cup-winning captain stands at the main entrance to Wembley Stadium.
whyItMatters: One of the most prominent football statues in the world, greeting every visitor to England's national stadium.
whereToFind: Wembley Stadium, London (permanent public installation)

title: United Trinity
creator: Philip Jackson
subject: club
subjectName: Manchester United's George Best, Denis Law and Bobby Charlton
logline: A bronze statue depicting United's three Ballon d'Or winners embracing in celebration of the 1968 European Cup win.
whyItMatters: One of the most photographed football statues in the world, marking a defining trio in Manchester United's history.
whereToFind: Old Trafford, Manchester (permanent public installation)
